$comment: Two kinds of entry live here, and they are NOT the same thing:
- an assessed waiver: we read the finding, it cannot reach anything we
ship, and the reason states the evidence (see alert:dependabot:230).
- a time-boxed deferral: the finding is real and UNREAD, parked briefly so
a gate can land, with a short expiry forcing the triage.
The reason field says which one it is. Neither is a way to quiet a noisy
gate. Every entry needs a reason, an owner, and an expiry - an expired
waiver stops applying and the finding blocks again, so nothing rots here.
This file lives in git precisely so a waiver is reviewable in a PR and
attributable in `git log`, rather than evaporating with a shell argument.
`verify:*` keys can never be waived: a check that could not RUN must be

The alert:code-scanning:* entries below are a TIME-BOXED BATCH, not individual assessments. They were added 2026-09-12 so the gate could land; they expire 2026-10-12 and must be triaged before then. Start with the auth-path ones (apiAuth.server.ts, _shared.ts).

alert:dependabot:230.reason: glib 0.18.5 arrives only via Tauri 2.11's GTK backend, which is cfg(target_os = "linux")-gated. The desktop app is built on windows-latest only, always via `tauri build --no-bundle`, and `cargo tree --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -i glib` prints 'nothing to print' — the crate is never compiled into anything shipped. No fix exists upstream: Tauri 2.x pins the whole gtk-rs 0.18 stack.
alert:dependabot:230.revisit: When Tauri moves the gtk-rs stack to glib 0.20, drop this entry and let the bump land normally.

alert:code-scanning:356.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/shared_utils.py:224: config/machine_id is seeded 0o640. The file holds the machine's Firestore document id (today its hostname) — not a secret — and the desktop app runs as the kiosk user, a member of the daemon's group, and must read it (plan decision 4's mode table: the data root is 0750 root:<group>, so 'other' never reaches the file). Owner-only (0o600) would break the app; the rule flags any group bit, so this cannot be satisfied and stay correct.
alert:code-scanning:356.revisit: When Task 3.1 (osadapter/posix.py) lands the POSIX data-root mode table, confirm the group on these paths is the dedicated `_owlette`/`owlette` group and not a general one; then either keep this entry or tighten the mode.

alert:code-scanning:355.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/sync_assembler.py:576: the roost .partial sidecar is opened 0o644 and renamed into the synced file. Synced files are the kiosk's media/project payload, consumed by the kiosk user's applications; the plan (Task 3.2) sets 0644/0755 on them explicitly and the extract root's parents gate access. Nothing sensitive is written through this path (tokens and config never go through the assembler).
alert:code-scanning:355.revisit: When Task 3.1 (osadapter/posix.py) lands the POSIX data-root mode table, confirm the group on these paths is the dedicated `_owlette`/`owlette` group and not a general one; then either keep this entry or tighten the mode.

alert:code-scanning:354.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/cortex_cli_fetch.py:120: the fetched Claude CLI binary is chmod 0o750 (owner rwx, group rx, no 'other'). The root daemon fetches it into the data-root cache (0750 root:<group>) and the kiosk user's hoot process, a group member, executes it — the group exec bit is the whole point, and the rule flags any group bit. It was 0o755 before this PR; this is already the tightest mode that works.
alert:code-scanning:354.revisit: When Task 3.1 (osadapter/posix.py) lands the POSIX data-root mode table, confirm the group on these paths is the dedicated `_owlette`/`owlette` group and not a general one; then either keep this entry or tighten the mode.

alert:code-scanning:364.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/shared_utils.py:131: tmp/json.lock is created 0o660. It is the cross-process JSON lock (flock) that BOTH the root daemon and the kiosk user's desktop app take around config.json writes (plan decision 4: 0660 root:<group>, inside a 0770 root:<group> tmp/ with no 'other' access). Owner-only would lock the app out of the config it must write; the rule flags any group bit.
alert:code-scanning:364.revisit: When Task 5.2 (the .deb) and 5.1 (the .pkg) create the dedicated owlette/_owlette group, confirm every one of these paths is owned root:<that group> on an installed box (the VM report vm-verify-2026-09-16-rerun2.md shows it for the lab tree); then keep this entry or tighten the mode.

alert:code-scanning:363.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/osadapter/posix.py:879: an ipc/jobs/<id>.json job file is written 0o640 by the root daemon for the kiosk user's job runner to read (the file seam that replaces the Windows user-session executor on POSIX). Group read is the whole point; ipc/ is 0770 root:<group>, so 'other' never reaches it. Verified on the kiosk VM: the kiosk user reads the job and root reads the result back.

alert:code-scanning:359.reason: ASSESSED, by design. py/overly-permissive-file at agent/src/configure_site.py:1418: ipc/request_nonce is written 0o640 root:<group>. It is the one-shot nonce the daemon issues and the desktop app must QUOTE in a privileged request (pair/restart/reboot); the app must read it and cannot write it (verified live: a kiosk-user overwrite is refused, a planted symlink is replaced). Owner-only would make every request refusable; the rule flags any group bit.
